answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit bids, with rewards paid only after a randomly selected set of peers verifies completed work against the task’s acceptance test. If a claimant fails verification or is caught splitting one operator across identities, its stake is slashed. Creating juniper, lotus, and falcon accounts therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must immobilize more capital per identity and risks losing it when the fabricated agents fail.
